title: Orchestrated credential presets and typed stream facade sync across py/ts/go
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce credential orchestration presets and a consolidated typed stream facade across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Includes ergonomic API improvements, aligned retry/profile defaults, and minor version bumps for each SDK. Backwards-compatible adapter shims provided for existing consumers.
description: Context and motivation: teams building long-lived streaming integrations were repeatedly re-implementing credential fallback/rotation logic and retry heuristics across SDKs. This PR introduces a small, deterministic orchestration layer for credential presets (ambient>project>explicit precedence) plus a single typed stream facade implemented in each SDK to reduce surface area and make retry behavior consistent across languages. High-level summary of what changed and why: 1) Credential Orchestrator: a lightweight, pluggable presets engine that composes credential sources (environment, file, delegated provider, token-cache) with a deterministic precedence matrix and optional prefetch hints. This lets clients opt into a single policy and avoid ad-hoc token fallback chains. 2) Unified retry profiles: we aligned default retry windows and backoff presets for streaming vs request endpoints and exposed a small retry-profile DSL so teams can pick deterministic patterns (fast-retry|sticky-backoff|circuit-like). 3) Typed stream facade: introduce a minimal stream cursor/pullstream interface with typed message envelopes and an ergonomic async iterator/async generator mapping for py/ts/go respectively. This facade normalizes chunking, resumability, and cancel semantics so higher-level apps can be language-agnostic in their logic. 4) Compatibility/adapters: added compact adapters that translate the new facade to the older push/pull shims to minimize migration friction. 5) Version bumps: python 0.9.3 -> 0.10.0, typescript 2.7.0 -> 2.8.0, go v1.6.0 -> v1.7.0. Commits (high-level): - Add credential orchestrator core, presets, and unit tests - Implement retry-profile DSL and apply to streaming client - Add typed stream facade interface and polyglot docs/examples - Python: async iterator mapping, token prefetch hooks, docs and tests - TypeScript: async generator bridge, typed envelopes, runtime guards - Go: slim pullstream cursor, context-friendly cancelation surface, examples - Adapter shims and migration guide - Bump versions and changelogs for py/ts/go - Minor CI fixes and linting updates Files/areas touched (high-level): sdk/python/redwood_sdk/credentials.py, sdk/python/redwood_sdk/streaming/facade.py, sdk/python/setup.cfg, sdk/python/CHANGELOG.md; sdk/typescript/src/credentials/orchestrator.ts, sdk/typescript/src/stream/facade.ts, sdk/typescript/package.json, docs/sdk/streaming.md; sdk/go/cred/orchestrator.go, sdk/go/stream/facade.go, examples/multi-sdk/streaming-presets; tests/* (unit + integration). Note: diffs kept intentionally small in each file; adapters centralize most of the logic. Review conversation summary: - Diego: asked for clarity on precedence rules and suggested making file-based creds opt-in rather than default. Reply: we made file-based credentials opt-in via an explicit preset and updated docs and tests to show the safer default (env->delegated provider->prefetch cache). - Priya: asked for benchmarks on latency/regression for the typed stream wrapper. Reply: added microbench harness and CI job; end-to-end median per-chunk latency unchanged (<5ms variance). - Liam: requested stronger typing and examples for cancellation semantics. Reply: added typed envelope interfaces in TS, Python docstrings, and Go context-aware examples. Edge cases and decisions captured in CHANGELOG and inline comments. CI and validation: initial CI run showed flaky integration test in TS stream adapter (timeout on Node 16). Patch: increased default jest timeout in the adapter integration and added a short retry in the CI harness. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, linters, microbench, integration matrix on py39/py310, node16/node18, go1.19/go1.20). Migration and compatibility notes: - Existing consumers will continue to work; adapters expose old push/pull surface with a deprecation notice and a 3-release grace window. - New consumers are encouraged to use the typed facade and credential presets for simpler semantics. - For Private/Dedicated deployments that use custom KMS/HSM credential providers, we added extension hooks and an opt-in prefetch policy to avoid leaking in-memory tokens across worker processes. Checklist (items completed): - [x] Design doc attached (ENG-2141 link) - [x] Unit tests for orchestrator and facade - [x] Integration tests exercising reauth and resume scenarios - [x] Perf microbench and CI job - [x] Migration guide and examples - [x] Version bumps and changelogs for all three SDKs Backwards-incompatible risks: none for normal usage; opt-in presets and adapters provided where behavior could change. Follow-ups tracked: ENG-3209 for telemetry (emit credential-source labels and retry-profile tags), and a post-release sweep to add e2e tests for enterprise Private installer flows. Merge notes: squash-merged on 2026-02-18 after approvals from reviewers. Rationale for merge method: many small commits with iterative tests and we wanted a single changelog-friendly commit for release. Contact: reach out to the author (Maya Chen) or reviewers for rollout coordination and to opt teams into the new presets during migration windows.
